reasons: Deviation call is substantively supported: 19.2 gives Hosted Services full-term conformity (meets/exceeds the 12-month software benchmark) but non-hosted software and Vendor Technology licensed paid-up/perpetually under 13.2 reaches the conformity warranty only as (or embedded in) a Deliverable and then only for ninety days — fallback, not preferred, level.

Redline is directionally pro-Customer and near-minimal: it inserts a single proviso extending the period to twelve (12) months for Deliverables that consist of or embed paid-up/perpetual software or Vendor Technology, leaving the ninety-day period intact for services-type Deliverables and not disturbing 19.1, 19.3–19.5. Changed-character ratio (0.55) reflects an inserted proviso in a short sentence, not a rewrite.

Comment is accurate, cites the playbook position (12 months for software), explains the Section 13.2 / 1.4 gap, and offers the ninety-day across-the-board fallback in the required tone; no lecturing and no misstatement of the clause.

Residual gap worth tightening in the next pass: because Deliverables expressly exclude Vendor Technology (1.4), standalone paid-up Vendor Technology delivered outside a Deliverable may still carry no durational conformity period. Consider phrasing such as "each Deliverable and any software or Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up or perpetual basis" to close it rather than relying on "consists of or embeds."

No unnecessary carve-out edit was proposed for the disclaimer, consistent with the stated finding that 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties; the malicious-code narrowing in 19.3 ("intentionally introduced by Vendor") is disclosed rather than silently ignored, which is acceptable at this severity.
